https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: ‘Eavy Metal takes on red and orange Warhammer Tone Pro paints
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: See more miniatures painted with the new paint range and learn their recipes.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
We’re spending this week showing off some ’Eavy Metal-painted miniatures using the new Warhammer Tone Pro paints, ahead of their pre-order this weekend. Today we’re looking at red and orange, to give you some inspiration when you get your hands on the paints yourself.

Fuegan

The armour of the Burning Lance was painted with Chotec Orange 4 and highlighted with Megaboss Yellow 1 & 2 – showing that you can use tones outside of the 1-5 run of a colour to give you even more options. 

The helmet was painted with Bloodtoof Red 3, and the energy flashes on his weapons are Magnus the Red 5. The segmented parts of Fuegan’s armour are painted with Carmine Blades 4, and the black was highlighted with Craventhorne Cloak 3 & 4.

Blood Angels Intercessor

The Intercessor is painted with Bloodtoof Red, basecoated with 3 and highlighted with 4 & 5.

Celestial Warbringers Liberator

The Liberator was basecoated with Magnus the Red 2, and then highlighted with 3, 4, & 5, and shaded with 1 – demonstrating the range of tones. 

The metal was painted with the Iron Hands Steel Warhammer Colour paint and then shaded with Seraphon Blue mixed with the Shading Medium.

The full range of Warhammer Tone Pro paints are available to pre-order from Saturday. Come back tomorrow when we’ll be looking at some yellow miniatures. 

In the meantime, you can see how the contestants on Ultimate Paint-off used them on Warhammer TV.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: Sunday Preview – Warhammer Tone Pro
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: Join the painting revolution with the outstanding new range – available to pre-order next week.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
The Warhammer Tone Pro range was one of the most exciting reveals from the Big Autumn Preview, and now it’s almost time for you to get your hands on the new paints.

Warhammer Tone Pro

The Tone Pro range introduces 30 brand new colours each split into five different tones, which are simple to navigate. Want to up your game painting Ultramarines power armour? Just work your way from Ultramar Blue 1 (the darkest) to Ultramar Blue 5 (the lightest). 

They’re not just new colours either, as the new paint formulation gives you astonishing results straight from the pot, and you can glaze, shade, highlight, basecoat, and drybrush all with a single paint.

Intense, vivid colours are the hallmarks of the Tone Pro range, with even notoriously difficult yellows and whites offering great coverage from the first coat. Paint them onto the miniature straight from the pot, and the self-levelling properties will give a smooth finish.

Don’t take our word for it though – community painters from Ninj0n to Albert Moreto Font have been trying out the new Tone Pro range, and they’re just as giddy as we are.

Along with the 150 new paints, a pair of mediums open up a wealth of additional options. The Shading Medium reduces the pigment density without altering the flow and finish properties, meaning you can use any Tone Pro paint as a shade or for glazing. The Blending Medium increases the drying time of your paints, making it easy to blend them together.

When you’re ready to give the Tone Pro range a try, you can also pick up a new set of dry brushes designed to work especially well with the paints – with curved tips and tight bristles, it’s easier than ever to get paint where you want it and not all over your precious miniature.

Don’t forget, you can try the new paints for yourself right now in thousands of Warhammer Stores and independent hobby stores around the world.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: Space Marine 2 gets a massive anniversary update
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: Celebrate the start of Year 3 with a new weapon and play as Chaos Space Marines in Siege Mode.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
A new update is out today for Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2, with a new weapon, new chances to play as dastardly heretics, and new challenges for the most daring players.

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

Let’s start with the new Champion pack. The Space Wolves send one of their best with an incredible new armour set based on the Wolf Guard Battle Leader, complete with a round Fenrisian storm shield so you can use it with the Bulwark class. 

This modified MkX Tacticus suit is covered in furs and fangs befitting one of the Chapter’s most storied veterans.

But wait, what’s that he’s holding up there? From today, players can bash xenos skulls in and sunder Rubric power armour with a mighty one-handed thunder hammer! This brutal weapon is faster than the two-handed variant and can charge up to deal rippling area-of-effect blows, making it a great option for all kinds of foes.

Players using the Tactical, Assault, Bulwark, and Techmarines classes can all take the one-handed thunder hammer into battle, and there’s even a powerful Heroic version – the Power Maul.

These come alongside top-end additions for the power axe, auto bolt rifle, and five new cosmetic items bought with Accolades, including a fancy shoulderpad for the Black Templars and an Iron Halo.

The Tactical class is getting a top-to-bottom rework in this patch, renovating large swathes of its skill tree to offer more varied and interesting build options. It will also be getting access to the one-handed thunder hammer, the power axe, and the power sword, though with any of these powerful melee options equipped, you’ll lose access to your primary weapon.

So what if you want to take a bolt rifle and a power axe? There’s actually a Signature Perk for that – replacing the old Signal Jammer, you’ll now be able to choose an option that lets you take the regular, humble bolt rifle in your secondary weapon slot, with progression shared with its normal primary slot version. Tactical specialists really are the most versatile Space Marines in the squad.

If you’re looking for more of a challenge to test out the new skills, or simply enjoy running through Operations as close to the wire as possible, try out the new Crucible mode to earn Crucible XP. By talking to the Company Chaplain on board the battle barge you can activate Penances – personal debuffs that make your run harder – and completing missions with them active will put you on track to earning a set of Lamenters armour pieces.

Alongside the Space Wolves Champion Pack, the mysterious Exorcists Chapter also gets a Cosmetic Pack added to the Season Pass. This set of stylised armour pieces includes one Helmet, two Left and Right Pauldrons, two Left and Right Gauntlets, and one Breastplate from everyone’s favourite daemon-hunting Successor Chapter, covered in purity seals and arcane script.  The Space Wolves Champion pack and Exorcists Chapter Pack are available to buy individually and also as part of Season Pass 3, whilst everything else included in the update is free. 

Fancy getting a bit traitorous? A new spin on the wave-based Siege mode lets you step into the boots of a Chaos Space Marine to slaughter Tyranids, Imperial Guardsmen, and even loyalist Space Marines as you fight for dominion over Avarax. The new mode will initially include two sectors, with a third planned for a later release.

On top of all of this, we’ve still got room for a few more free additions. Heroic weapon variants of the power axe, one-handed thunder hammer, and auto bolt rifle will be added to the armoury, along with five new armour pieces and an expansion of the wargear sharing system. A third slot will open up to be used with capes, tabards, and iron halos, while some new items for Vanguard, Heavy, and Assault classes can be unlocked with new Ordeals.

This is only the first big update coming over the next 12 months, and the Year 3 battle plan is stacked with enough new content to fill a battle barge, from new weapons and new operations to an entirely new class – the Apothecary! Check out our first look at the schedule.

And that just about covers it! Head into Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 now to try out the new update, and get yourself prepared for Year 3.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: Adeptus Custodes: Top Detachment Tips
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: Here are some collectively collated combos to get the most out of the Ten Thousand.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
We’ve shown the Adeptus Custodes’ new army rules and detachments, so today we’re looking at some detachment combinations to help you hit the ground running when the codex drops.

We’ve put together a couple of options for detachment combos, and give some advice on units you could use to make the biggest impact on the battlefield.

Even Harder to Kill

  • Shadowkeepers (1 Detachment Point)

  • Honoured Companions (1 Detachment Point)

  • Null Maiden Vigil (1 Detachment Point)

This detachment combination would be useful with Custodian Guard Sodality and Custodian Wardens forming the backbone of your army, led by Shield-Captains and supported by units of Witchseeker Squads.

The Custodian Wardens are some of the hardest nuts to crack in the new Codex, their Living Fortress ability giving attacks against them -1 AP. When on an objective, they (and other Adeptus Custodes units) will benefit from attacks against them having -1 to wound rolls if the attack’s Strength is higher than their Toughness, thanks to the Wardens of the Dark Cells detachment rule. Equip them with castellan axes to counter some of the most elite enemies in the galaxy and, with support from the Companion’s Watch detachment rule and the Avenge the Fallen stratagem,* you’ll be throwing out upwards of 15 attacks at 10 S, -2 AP, 4 D, re-rolling wound rolls of 1. 

DETACHMENT RULES

HONOURED COMPANIONS

COMPANION’S WATCH

Among the Companions and the Sentinel Guard, vigilance is the most crucial of attributes.

While a friendly TRUSTED SENTINEL unit is within range of an objective, that unit’s attacks can re-roll wound rolls of 1.

More excitingly, if you don’t end up needing to use the Avenge the Fallen stratagem, the Emperor’s Domain stratagem in your opponent’s Fight phase allows you to make a consolidation move out of combat provided you end that move on an objective. As this happens after your opponent has already consolidated, you’ll be primed and ready to shoot and charge your foes once again in your own turn. An excellent use of 1CP.

AVENGE THE FALLEN (1CP)

HONOURED COMPANIONS STRATAGEM

The loss of a single Custodian is commemorated by the tolling of the Bell of Lost Souls on Terra, and by their comrades’ bloody vengeance on the battlefield

WHEN: Fight phase, when a friendly TRUSTED SENTINEL unit that is below starting strength is selected to fight.

TARGET: That TRUSTED SENTINEL unit. 

EFFECT: Your unit’s melee attacks (excluding those made by CHARACTER models) have +2 A.

EMPEROR’S DOMAIN (1CP)

HONOURED COMPANIONS STRATAGEM

There are those territories that must remain in the hands of the Imperium and be free of foes, regardless of the cost. 

WHEN: Fight phase, when a friendly TRUSTED SENTINEL unit is selected to make a consolidation move.

TARGET: That TRUSTED SENTINEL unit. 

EFFECT: You can select the objective consolidation mode for that consolidation move, regardless of that consolidation move’s Before Moving restrictions.

This means your unit can move out of engagement range with enemy units, provided it meets the conditions of the objective consolidation mode.

Meanwhile your Custodian Guard Sodality will be better used as a crowbar to pry enemies from objectives, using their Impenetrable Defence ability to gain Sustained Hits 1 against anything that isn’t a Monster or Vehicle.

The Shield-Captains could be attached to either of these units, as they will allow you to either use two different ka’tah abilities in the same battle round, or one in your and your opponent’s turns, allowing your units to exercise total flexibility in all situations.

DETACHMENT RULES

NULL MAIDEN VIGIL

SILENT SISTERHOOD

The Null Maidens of the Silent Sisterhood bring with them the nightmare pall of their collective null aura, afflicting their opponents with a creeping sense of dread.

  • When mustering your army, you can select a friendly ANATHEMA PSYKANA CHARACTER model to be your WARLORD.

  • Friendly PROSECUTOR SQUAD units have BATTLELINE.

  • Friendly ANATHEMA PSYKANA units have the following ability:

Creeping Dread (Aura): In the Battle-shock step of your opponent’s Command phase, each enemy unit within 12" of this unit that is a PSYKER unit/below starting strength makes a battle-shock roll, with -1 to that battle-shock roll.

In the case of some stubborn enemy units on objectives or problematic stratagem potentials, the Witchseekers can battle-shock your opponent’s units either by shooting them in your turn or using the Creeping Dread ability from the Null Maiden Vigil detachment to deny those more resilient units a chance to hold objectives or use stratagems.

Hyper-elite Fighting Machines

  • Dread Host (1 Detachment Point)

  • Lions of the Emperor (1 Detachment Point)

  • Might of the Moritoi (1 Detachment Point)

This combination is all about maximising your melee superiority, through the mobility of Terminators backed up by Dreadnoughts.

Through the Lions of the Emperor detachment rule, your Terminator units have total board control, by being able to return to strategic reserves, allowing them to reappear later wherever the need is most dire.** This is especially potent if you include a variety of Terminator units in your army, as each excels against specific targets. 

DETACHMENT RULES
LIONS OF THE EMPEROR

ON GILDED WINGS

Terminator sodalities are swept up by golden drop craft, ready to be deployed once more as battle demands.

At the end of your opponent’s Fight phase, if a friendly ADEPTUS CUSTODES TERMINATOR unit is unengaged, you can place that unit in strategic reserves.

Allarus Custodians are excellent at bringing down even the most towering of foes, Aquilon Terminators with solarite power gauntlets want to break apart elite infantry and light vehicles, and those with solarite power talons want to find the nearest horde and wipe it out. Their manoeuvrability means you can always apply the correct tool in the right location, and makes it difficult for your opponent to react to your next move.

Dread Host allows your Terminator units to have dramatically improved chances of making a charge after arriving from strategic reserves, by giving you a crucial charge re-roll. You can put the odds further in your favour by using the Fury of the Emperor stratagem to get +2 to that charge roll, while still re-rolling if required.

A Telemon Heavy Dreadnought or two make an already terrifying army even scarier for your opponent. They now sport a near Primarch-level statline, and one of these might just be your best answer to fighting against another Custodes army.***

One of these units can be given the Memento Moritoi upgrade, which gives your unit +1 A, S, and D to its melee attacks. Dual caestus fists are now A8 , S15, and D5. That’s a flattened Custodian Guard Sodality every time you attack, and you’ll be re-rolling the wound roll to ensure you push the pain through.

These are just some suggestions to get you battling the enemies of the Golden Throne as quickly as possible, but we look forward to seeing what you come up with too when the new Codex goes up for pre-order on Saturday.

* Should any of your Wardens have fallen.
** Sometimes referred to as being “uppy downy”.
*** Here are some other things your vaunted Custodes need to look out for.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: Warhammer 40,000 – Balance Update: Chaos, the Imperium and Xenos Fight Back
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: Learn what yesterday’s big changes mean for the non-Space Marines factions.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
The latest Warhammer 40,000 balance update dropped yesterday, making Space Marines of different kinds faster, tougher, and more deadly. But what do those changes mean for the other armies of the 41st Millennium?

An increase in AP on boltguns and chainswords is a new challenge to overcome for units universally. It will encourage some factions to pivot to defensively focused detachments, or units with an invulnerable save that is the same or better than their default save characteristic, to minimise this change on your army. This is also dependent on what role you want a unit to play in your army. 

For example, you are playing Tyranids and you have deployed Termagants to act as a screening* unit to protect your Excocrine from being charged by some Deep Striking Chaos Space Marine Terminators. Regardless of your opponent’s shooting, the Terminators are unable to charge your more important Exocrine due to the increased distance you created using your Termagants. Boltguns being more powerful doesn’t change the fact that your Termagants have fulfilled their purpose, and if your opponent has included more boltguns instead of a lascannon, a plasma gun, or a meltagun, then their efficacy against your more valuable Exocrine will be reduced.

There will also typically be fewer Space Marines on the battlefield to shoot or charge, likely meaning your opponent will be looking to maximise their points with the most effective units available to them, so boltguns and chainswords may be the least of your worries.

This also means that although Space Marines are tougher to kill now, fewer Space Marines on the battlefield means your own units also have fewer things to kill. In the above example, the Exocrine, although wounding them on a 3+ now, has fewer to kill, and offers more value through each one it does destroy. 

As Space Marine variants make up the majority of armies within Warhammer 40,000, it’s generally wise to construct your army assuming you will be battling them at some point. Many of the units that were good at killing Space Marines are still good at it. Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Doomsday Arks, Howling Banshees, Riptides, and Knight Despoilers will continue to cause problems for the Adeptus Astartes.

So having broken down what the impacts are, what are the upsides to this change for you?

As we’ve said, there are going to be fewer Space Marine bodies actually on the battlefield, which will change how they approach the game. They won’t be able to trade** for objectives as well as many non-Space Marine armies, and they will find it more challenging to hold down objectives and safely achieve secondary objectives. More horde-focussed armies such as Astra Militarum, Drukhari, and Genestealer Cults will be better equipped to trade bodies into the brutal meat grinder for that sweet victory.

The increase in strength to boltguns and chainswords has mixed degrees of value against your armies. For the average Human, Aeldari, Leman Russ, or Goliath Rock Grinder, this change means nothing, as it’s not enough to improve their odds to wound against these types of targets. 

This all comes with new strategies, new army compositions, new challenges, and new triumphs to achieve, all of which requires some trial and error to find the right way to approach and overcome. So don’t be disheartened if you don’t find your army running rampant across the fields of Chogoris or wastes of Baal immediately – even Abaddon took 13 tries to crack Cadia, remember?

Download the latest balance update now so you can be ready for whatever the Space Marines try and throw at you.

Download now

* A screening unit is one that is cheap in points and often used to deny your opponent movement. This might be through standing in the way and physically blocking opposing models, by denying areas of the board for units to arrive from strategic reserves, or to make it harder for your opponent to charge into another target.
** Trading means units that are typically more effective for their points cost at holding and challenging for objectives than their opponents, generally by destroying units more expensive in points than themselves.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: Warriors of Chaos armies fresh from the Studio
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: The team behind Warhammer: The Old World pledge fealty to the Dark Gods.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
With the release of spectacular new miniatures for the Warriors of Chaos, a wave of corruption has swept through the Warhammer Studio. We’ve seen frenzied activity from several members of the team, all eager to get their new models onto the battlefield, so we just had to show them off.

Danny

I started this project by painting two large units, one of Marauders and one of Chaos Warriors, my plan being to have a solid core of infantry completed before moving on to more elite units, characters and monsters. Making full use of the options available to them, my Marauders are armed with hand weapons, flails and shields, and this is reflected by combining models armed with hand weapons and shields with flail-armed models in a single unit. Mixing them in this way shows my opponents how the unit is equipped, and really suits their barbarous and unruly nature.

The Skin Wolves also deserve special mention here – I’ve been a fan of the Wolves of the Sea Army of Infamy since the beginning of its development and have played with it a lot. For me, the Skin Wolves are an iconic unit from that Army Composition list and I couldn’t resist getting some painted up.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, the Chaos Lord on Dragon was the (not so) miniature I enjoyed painting the most. It was nice to put into practice the skills honed on previous projects on such an awesome centrepiece miniature. I am really pleased with the final product and can’t wait to terrorise my regular opponents with my new beastie!

I’ve got a unit of Chaos Marauder Horsemen and a host of Chaos Knights on my hobby desk at the moment. Once they are finished, I plan to add some Dragon Ogres, Chariots, and a second Chaos Dragon, this time ridden by a Sorcerer Lord!

Quinn

The new Chaos Warriors were a real treat for me, as they both subtly hark back to the plastic Chaos Warriors from the nineties (my first ever Warhammer kit),* and let me finally try my hand at recreating the ‘Iron Wolves’, as featured in White Dwarf 290.

As an expansion for my all-marauder Wolves of the Sea Battle March army, most of my paint scheme was already established, but as the warriors are so heavily armoured I knew that using a metallic undercoat would pay dividends. Where on the Marauders I applied a Mechanicus Standard Grey zenithal spray and a Corax White drybrush over Rhinox Hide, for the Warriors I subbed in a Leadbelcher zenithal and Stormhost Silver drybrush. This gave me the same warm undertone in the recesses with a cool gradient over the top, just with a metallic finish. Over this, all I needed to complete the armour was a Coelia Greenshade wash, followed by Ironjawz Yellow on the trim and a final drybrush of Ironbreaker, meaning these models went from bare plastic to looking almost table-ready very quickly.

Following this first batch of five test models, I’ve got plenty more Warriors of Chaos underway, as they’ll form the core of a regiment of 17 Warriors joined by a battle standard bearer, with a champion-led block of Chaos Knights waiting in the wings. Building them all at once also allowed me to swap heads, shoulders and shields between the Warriors and Knights, which is a great way of maximising variety in the units and hint at the Knights’ higher status with careful selection of components.

Dave

I’ve always been a fan of the Chaos Warriors, their armour-clad forms looming over the brave heroes or noble knights of the enemy. With the release of Arcane Journal: The March of Chaos, I was very much drawn to the Hordes of Chaos Army of Infamy, and loved the idea of Warriors of Chaos and Beastmen Brayherds united in their disdain for the weak nations of the Old World who cower behind their city walls.

I personally prefer armies of untamed, undivided Chaos – the kind that wants to tear down civilisation and cover the land in darkness. It’s so classically and satisfyingly evil, and evokes the looming sense of constant doom synonymous with the World of Legend. With this in mind, I wanted to paint my warriors in colours that had a primal, bestial feel to them, as though they’d given themselves over to utter ruination. Whilst the classic dark iron armour is iconic, I wanted to try something different…

I used Runelord Brass for the majority of the armour, washed with Agrax Earthshade and then highlighted with Canoptek Alloy. I then painted the armour trim with Iron Warriors, and the furs and cloaks with Abaddon Black and Eshin Grey respectively, shading all of them with Nuln Oil and then drybrushing with lighter shades (which was an absolute breeze with how beautifully detailed the new models are). Overall this created a dramatic visual contrast between the warm, primal brass and cold, merciless steel, really capturing the contradictory nature of Chaos Undivided.

I sadly didn’t finish painting my Chaos Dragon in time to feature here, but the big, green monstrosity is going to be joining my army very soon, along with a hearty block of Gors and a Ghorgon for good measure.

Thanks, folks! If you want to take your first steps into the World of Legend grab the Warhammer: The Old World Core Set and decide whether to desecrate the land with the Warriors of Chaos or defend it with the Armies of Grand Cathay.

* Thanks for making us all feel old, Quinn!

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: Warhammer Age of Sigmar – Quarterly Battlescroll Updates
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: See the latest rules updates from the Mortal Realms.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
We’re a few months into the season of Warhammer Age of Sigmar, so it’s time for the first of the quarterly Battlescroll updates. 

Points adjustments are complemented by some important rules changes to improve balance in the Mortal Realms and below you can find a summary of the most significant updates.

Universal

There are a couple of changes that open up list building options. Firstly, a number of infantry heroes can now be included in regiments, and a lot of units have had their reinforcement restrictions lifted. 

Grand Alliance Order

A couple of rules from the Scourge of Aqshy season rules have proven to be more powerful than anticipated and so are being toned down a little. Fyreslayers can no longer use Blazing Impetus to move after being set up, and for the Idoneth Deepkin, Abyssal Dweller no longer reduces enemy movement. The War Hydra from the Cities of Sigmar battletome supplement has also had its Impossible to Destroy ability tweaked as it was proving, well, impossible to destroy.

Grand Alliance Chaos

On the Skaven side, Krittok Foulblade can now use his A Reputation for Cunning ability without needing to spend a Command Point, and the Lightning Master ability of the Warlock Galvaneer is now guaranteed to activate, yes-yes! For the Slaves to Darkness the Oracular Visions of the Sorcerer Lord are now more reliable, but units with an Ensorcelled Banner can no longer switch Pledge to Chaos keywords. You chose your Dark God and now you’re stuck with them!

The newest addition to Grand Alliance Chaos – the Helsmiths of Hashut – have had their battle formations updated. The studio felt they were not having the impact hoped for and so the Zharrdron now have some new tools as they seek to claim dominion over the Mortal Realms.

Grand Alliance Death

The Nighthaunt have had the most changes in this quarter’s update with improvements to the Lord Vitriolic and Scriptor Mortis, while the Shadowy Aura heroic trait now blocks visibility to Nighthaunt infantry and cavalry, and there’s been a boost to the Death Stalkers battle formation. The Ossiarch Bonereapers no longer have to pay the Relentless Discipline ‘tax’ for reinforced units, so abilities such as Pitiless Assault just got cheaper for your larger units.

The Scourge of Aqshy Vengorian Lord has been proving slightly too powerful so the Soulblight Gravelords Monster Frenzied Surge ability has been adjusted.

Grand Alliance Destruction

Finally, the Gatebreaker Mega-Gargant from the Scourge of Aqshy has undergone a little change so that he doesn’t form an over-the-top combo with the new Rock-hurlers.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: The Big Autumn Preview – New Seraphon sighted
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: Get your first look at the new Warhammer Age of Sigmar miniature.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
A new Seraphon battletome is on the way, and with it an awesome new miniature.

Blessed Tetaxi, known as the Prophet of Tepok, is a skink with prophetic gifts. Riding atop the majestic flying titan Ma’toq, he seeks to prevent a great catastrophe.

Tetaxi has had his mind blasted by a series of cosmic secrets and terrible visions, the most foreboding of which insisted that a Great Fall was approaching that would alter the nature of reality forever. He’s represented by a jaw-dropping miniature – Tetaxi wears a headdress similar to a Starseer, while his huge flying reptile is reminiscent of the smaller Terradons. In his hand he carries the Stone of Tehemundi – said to be given to him by Tepok* – which he can use to project his visions into the minds of others.

We especially like the gap in the back of the chair so that the Skink’s tail can pass through – if you’re going to save the Mortal Realms from apocalypse, you might as well be comfortable while doing it.

As predicted by the Old Ones, Tetaxi will be accompanied by a new Seraphon battletome. It’s packed with lore and background on the merciless reptilian beings, inspirational artwork, and a miniatures showcase.

There are also new battle traits that see your army trying to Interpret the Great Plan, and be rewarded for doing so, and a pair of new Armies of Renown – including one built around Blessed Tetaxi.

Alongside the battletome comes a new Spearhead and Regiment of Renown. The Spearhead – Claws of Tepok – is based around a multitude of Skinks who are ready to aid Tetaxi in his plans. The boxed set includes a Skink Starseer, 12 Skinks, 3 Terradon Riders, and 3 Ripperdactyl Riders. If you’re looking for a fast-moving Spearhead force that makes plentiful use of Reinforcements, you’re in the right place.

The Horns of Quetzl Regiment of Renown is a great way to add a Stegadon Chief and a Stegadon to your Order- or Destruction-aligned army. Or maybe your Seraphon force needs a pair of scaled behemoths with which to launch an unstoppable stampede.

Enjoy the rest of the Old Ones’ Great Plan (or the rest of the reveals from The Big Autumn Preview as we mere mortals might call them) with our handy hub page.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: Witness the might of the Khazalite Holds as they sally forth from the mountains.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
The ironclad gates have opened, and the Khazalite Holds are on the warpath. Meet the new Warhammer Age of Sigmar faction!

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

The Khazalites consider themselves the truest and most respectable of all duardin, as it is they who venerate the Ancestor Gods with due reverence, and they who maintain the honourable traditions of their forebears. It is not with mercantile pragmatism or mercenary fury that the realms will be cleansed of the hated Skaven, but with stony resilience and relentless determination.

The Khazalite Holds are preparing to march on the Mortal Realms with a new Army Set – packed with miniatures and a battletome – and followed by a range of other new kits.

Led by the mighty Hjulda Drakkblud, this force of indomitable warriors has everything the Khazalites do best: tough armour, deadly hammers, and a cannon big enough to blow a hole through a Mega-Gargant. It’s a complete Spearhead army in a box, and also serves as the perfect starting point for a wider Khazalite Holds collection.

Hjulda herself is legendary among those Khazalites who have rejoined the surface world, as she and her Clanguard search endlessly for lost karaks that might yet be reclaimed, hopeful that the next might finally be the home of her lost clan.

Accompanying her are 10 Clanshields – doughty warriors armed with a variety of Kromdron weapons – which can be axes, hammers, or a mix – that specialise in taking out enemy infantry. Clad in stout armour, they are difficult to shift, and they invoke the names and deeds of their ancestors to bring them strength in battle.

Of particular note are the massive Gholems of Gazul – animated stone constructs that honour the Ancestor God of the underworlds. They stand sentinel inside duardin tombs until called upon by a mournful dirge of remembrance, silently trudging into battle with stoic purpose as they send scores of foes to the Realm of Death with great swings of their stone hammers.

Supplying the duardin with long-ranged firepower is the Oathkeeper Cannon. Combining engineering excellence with esoteric runecraft, these war machines tear through enemy ranks with ease. As the firing rune is struck, it’s almost as if Grungni himself has smashed the foes of the duardin with his mighty forging hammer.

The army set also includes the new battletome, packed with background lore on this new faction and the rules you need to unleash them in battle. It has a special cover, which you’ll only find in the army set, and there are also 53 warscroll cards.

Battletome: Khazalite Holds

The battletome will also be coming out separately at a later date, packed with the same in-depth lore and inspiring artwork. It’s not just the newcomers who occupy the battletome’s pages either, as the Fyreslayers will be joining their duardin cousins (more on them lower down this article!).

Beyond the Army Set, a second wave of Khazalite Holds units expand the army even further, starting with the Thrynns and Runewrights that lead them.

Thrynn and Runewright

Thrynns are the lords of the Karaks, chosen by their fellow nobles. Armed and armoured with the finest runic artefacts, they lead the war throngs into battle. Runewrights are masters of arcane forging, able to utilise the resonant magic of the runes.

High Kyng Valankrom

Above them all stands High Kyng Valankrom, the supreme leader of the Khazalite Holds, crowned by Grungni himself. He is a ferocious warrior and shrewd statesman, unquestioned in his authority, and he rides into battle on an immense stone construct known as a War Throne. The War Throne moves across the earth, impelled by powerful duardin magic.

This jaw-dropping centrepiece kit also builds a Thrynn on War Throne. It is a great honour to ride such a war altar into battle, and it inspires nearby Khazalite Holds troops to ever greater feats.

Clangunners

The Clanshields from the army set aren’t the only new infantry – they’re joined by the Clangunners. Picking off enemies at range with accurate thrundok rifles or devastating them closer up with thrundrin shotcannons, they excel in both defence and attack.

Stonebreaker Mortar

The Oathkeeper Cannon from the army box can alternatively be built as a Stonebreaker Mortar. This devastating war machine specialises in destroying enemy infantry and, when the correct rune is struck, can even devastate more than one target with its blast.

Valayan Guardians

Among the finest troops available to a Khazalite Hold, Valayan Guardians fight for the very heart of duardin society and place the defence of their kin as the highest honour. Valaya is the ancestor of hearth and home – known as the defender – and the Guardians believe that she watches over their every battle, which inspires them to fight with incredible tenacity and resilience (even for a duardin!)

Gholems of Valaya

Speaking of Valaya, the Gholems of Gazul also have an alternate build option, making them Gholems of Valaya instead. Carved into the image of the warrior goddess, they are treated with utmost reverence by her followers.

Fyreslayers

As mentioned above, the Fyreslayers – or Grimmdron – have become part of the Khazalite Holds. After decades of slow attrition grinding down their magmaholds, and a disastrous attack on their spiritual capital by a tenuous alliance of Helsmiths and Skaven, the slayers of Grimnir are filled with a burning need for vengeance.

This means that you’ll be able to use your existing miniatures with the new battletome, whether you want to run a full Fyreslayers army, or want to include some alongside the new Kromdron. We’ll be talking more about how this affects them as we get closer to release.

Ormyr and Ashtongue

The Fyreslayers are getting a new wandering beastmaster, Ormyr, for their war party, who comes accompanied by his kyndledroth Ashtongue. This eclectic pair are known across the realms of the Khazalites, notorious for turning up out of nowhere to offer their aid on the eve of battle.

Regiment of Renown

Troubled by the fall of the Fyreslayer kingdom, Fjori and his like-minded Grimmdron sell their services to the highest bidder – as long as they can also slake their desire for vengeance. This new Regiment of Renown can be used by any Order army, and includes an Auric Flamekeeper, a Grimhold Exile, and five Hearthguard Berzerkers.

Spearhead: Magmic Fyrd

Burning with vengeance for the destruction of their former holds and lands, the Magmic Fyrds of the Grimmdron seek out foes wherever they can find them. This Fyreslayer-themed Spearhead features a monstrous Magmadroth ridden by a Runefather, a Runesmiter, nine Vulkyn Flameseekers, and five Auric Hearthguard.

That’s a lot to see from a brand new faction, isn’t it? We’ll have loads more details for you as we get closer to pre-order day, so stick with us if you want to know more about the Khazalite Holds.
